subject: GPU fleet provisioning — integration roadmap & regional priorities
messages:
From: Lucas Miller <lucas.m@archway.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: GPU fleet provisioning and regional choices

Jasmine —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We agreed Archway.ai will move forward with a Dedicated GPU pool for our inference workloads. Before legal and procurement start the paperwork, I wanted to map the practical onboarding timeline and regional choices so our infra team can align. High-level asks from our side:
- Primary region: us-west-2, fallback eu-west-1 (90% traffic in US).
- Autoscale behaviour: prefer fast burst to handle daily inference spikes (90th percentile burst to ~150% baseline for 15m windows).
- Latency target: p95 under 120ms for chat endpoints.

Can you share a proposed sprint plan, what you need from us (network, VPC peering, IP whitelists, SOC2 evidence), and any early gating items that would hold up activation? I attached a first-pass SOW and a capacity matrix.

Best,
Lucas
Sr. Infra Eng, Archway.ai
(attachment: Archway_SOW_v1.pdf)
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Lucas Miller <lucas.m@archway.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-11T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: GPU fleet provisioning and regional choices

Lucas —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick reply with next steps and what we'll own vs what we need from Archway: 
- Redwood will: provision dedicated pool (gpus pinned to vm families), set autoscale policy templates, validate p95 latency in staging, provide SOC2 artifact bundle.
- Archway will: confirm VPC CIDR ranges, open cidr for outbound to our Egress IPs, provide test data and the three representative endpoints you want proxied.

Proposed timeline (high level):
1) Week 0-1: network & security intake + legal review (we kick off DocuSign for SOW).
2) Week 2: staging provisioning in us-west-2, baseline tests.
3) Week 3: autoscale tuning (burst windows + queue thresholds).
4) Week 4: canary traffic + go/no-go to prod in us-west-2; eu-west-1 standby configuration.

I'll follow up with a technical playbook and a short checklist for netops. Monica, Ben — can you confirm pool sizing estimate from the capacity matrix and whether we need multi-instance types for faster burst?

Thanks,
Jasmine
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
(attachment: region_capacity_matrix.xlsx)
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: GPU fleet provisioning and regional choices

Jasmine / Ben / Logan —

Reviewed Archway's matrix. Notes and ops asks: 
- Recommended initial pool: 8 x A100-40GB equiv (will cover baseline ~12k tokens/min with room to burst).
- For fast burst behaviour we advise 2 warm standby instances (same family) plus policy to scale by +50% within 60s, cap burst at +150% sustained for 15m before cooldown.
- If Archway expects >200 concurrent streams at peak, we should add a mixed-architecture lane (one or two L40s) for short/latency-sensitive requests.

Netops checklist (what we need from Archway):
- VPC peering details and approved egress CIDRs (will provide our list).
- TLS cert / private key handling preferences (bring-your-own or Redwood-managed).
- Any specific compliance endpoints for auditing (HIPAA fields? we need to toggle retention).

Action: Ben to draft SLOs for latency/cost tradeoffs and Logan to assign an engineer for the staging cutover.

—Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lucas Miller <lucas.m@archway.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: archway-sales@archway.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: GPU fleet provisioning and regional choices

Thanks — this looks good. Two quick clarifications:
1) We can do BYO TLS certs; would prefer Redwood manage rotation if you support that.
2) Peak concurrency: we'll likely see short spikes to ~250 concurrent sessions for 3-5 minute bursts at launch (marketing push). If that materially changes sizing, we can earmark additional burst budget.

Also, legal asked for a single redline pass — sending the SOW comments via DocuSign. Once SOW is signed we'll provide the VPC details and test endpoints.

Lucas
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Lucas Miller <lucas.m@archway.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-14T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: GPU fleet provisioning and regional choices

Lucas —

Acknowledged. We'll adjust the burst cap to accommodate occasional 250-concurrency spikes (operationally: add one extra warm standby and broaden burst window to 20m with a stricter cooldown). Monica and Ben will mark the sizing change in the pool estimate and Logan will schedule the staging engineer for next Monday.

I'll watch for the signed DocuSign and the VPC info. Once we have both, we'll open the network intake ticket and target provisioning in us-west-2 on the following Tuesday.

Next steps (action owners):
- Lucas / Archway: sign SOW + provide VPC details (due 2027-06-16).
- Monica: update pool sizing workbook + SLO draft (due 2027-06-15).
- Logan: assign staging engineer and confirm cutover window (due 2027-06-15).

Thanks — looking forward to the launch.

Jasmine
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
--Quoted attachments referenced above: Archway_SOW_v1.pdf (summary page); region_capacity_matrix.xlsx (estimated RPS -> GPU mapping)--
